question.text: A bond portfolio has a sensitivity per basis point (PV01) of Rs. 45,000. The PV01 of the 10-year GOI bond futures contract is Rs. 900 per lot. How many lots should be shorted to hedge the portfolio?

explanation.text: The Logic: Hedge lots = portfolio sensitivity per bp / futures sensitivity per lot = Rs. 45,000 / Rs. 900 = 50 lots. PV01 is the rupee price change for a 1 bp yield move, so equating PV01s neutralises the impact of a small parallel shift. The Trap: 45 lots divides 45,000 by 1,000; 500 lots divides by 90; 20 lots divides by 2,250. The correct hedge uses the PV01 / PVBP per lot in the denominator. Note: The workbook flags two limitations of this duration-based hedge: it is an approximation that holds for small yield moves, and the portfolio and futures prices may not move in tandem, leaving residual basis risk.
